To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phase behavior of API/polymer solid dispersions can be predicted with PC-SAFT and that the thermodynamic properties of API/copolymeric solid dispersions are a function of the monomer type and the copolymer composition.
the thermodynamic properties of amorphous solid dispersions of poorly soluble drugs in copolymers can be tuned by the type of monomers and copolymer weight fraction.
the thermodynamic stability of solid dispersions of poorly soluble APIs in copolymer excipient is a function of the monomer type and the copolymer composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a thermodynamic model for predicting the thermodynamic phase behaviors of solid dispersions as a function of copolymer type and composition.
the thermodynamic phase diagram of amorphous solid dispersions of poorly soluble APIs and copolymer excipient.

the influence of monomer type (e.g., vinylpyrrolidon and vinylacetate) and the copolymer composition (e.g., the weight fraction of vinylpyrrollidone) on the phase behavior (e.g., glass-transition temperature) of solid dispersions of poorly soluble active pharmaceutically ingredients (APIs).

the glass transition temperature is not only a function of API and polymer but also of the polymer composition.

the glass-transition temperature of API/copolymeric excipient solid dispersions can be tuned by changing the monomer composition and that this effect can be predicted with the PC-SAFT equation of state.
